title: A Time-Reparameterized Cumulative Intensity Extrapolation Sampler for Discrete Flow Matching
claim: Our method keeps error low across evaluation budgets and beats existing samplers, with the largest gains when compute is most limited.
layout: 1 panel line plot, error versus log-scale budget, ours as thick red line
description: A single line chart titled 'Countdown Sequence Task'. The x-axis is NFE on a log2 scale (8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256). The y-axis is Error (%), from 0 to 16. Five methods are drawn with distinct markers and colors. Euler tau-leaping is a green dashed line with circles. Tweedie tau-leaping is a blue dashed line with squares. theta-RK2 is a purple solid line with triangles. theta-Trapezoidal is a cyan solid line with diamonds. TR-CIE (Ours) is a thick red solid line with large circles, listed in a boxed legend at top right. At NFE 8 the baselines start at about 12 to 14.5% error, while TR-CIE starts near 4%. All curves fall steeply as NFE grows. The red curve flattens near 2% from NFE 16 onward and stays below every baseline. The eye goes first to the thick red line along the bottom and to the steep drop on the left.
caption: Comparison on the synthetic countdown task. We compare our TR-CIE sampler with other samplers across various NFE. The error rate (lower is better) indicates that our method generally achieves better performance. We also observe that TR-CIE sampler significantly reduces errors especially in the low-NFE regime.
abstract: Discrete flow matching (DFM) provides a principled framework for generative modeling on discrete state spaces via continuous-time Markov chain dynamics. In practice, sampling for DFM commonly employs discretizations such as $Ï$-leaping, yet efficient sampling methods under a limited number of function evaluations (NFE) remain less studied. To address this gap, we propose the Time-Reparameterized Cumulative Intensity Extrapolation (TR-CIE) sampler, which aims to improve sampling quality when function evaluations are restricted. TR-CIE consists of two components. First, a schedule-based time reparameterization rescales the time grid according to the noise schedule. Under standard factorized DFM rate parameterizations, this transformation of variables absorbs the schedule-dependent growth term and mitigates stiffness near the terminal sampling stage. Second, we introduce a cumulative-intensity extrapolation updating rule. By reusing cached model outputs from the previous step as a history term, this improves the approximation of stepwise cumulative intensities on the resulting non-uniform time grid. We provide a theoretical analysis that bounds the local approximation error of cumulative intensities and establishes convergence results. The resulting sampler requires one NFE per step and introduces no additional model evaluations compared to the standard $Ï$-leaping sampler. Extensive experiments on synthetic tasks, text generation, and text-to-image benchmarks demonstrate that our method improves sampling quality under limited NFE.
